name: The Human Body & Health - very easy (AI-written, not yet reviewed)
description: 17 very easy questions on the human body and health, written by Claude on 2026-10-06 as the gentlest level of the 'The Human Body & Health' review pack: things almost everyone knows, in one short plain sentence, worded for adults. They are marked easy with a note "very easy" until the very easy level lands. The independent fact-check kept 17 of 17 written, fixed 3 and deleted 0. Every question and answer needs checking by a person before anybody plays it.

source.name: Written by hand by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) on 2026-10-06, from its own knowledge plus the pages each item cites: no API call. 15 items cite a page the writing pass fetched on 2026-10-06 and quote the phrase on it that supports the fact; 2 rest on "common knowledge" (genuinely universal everyday facts), each with the reason. Then fact-checked item by item by a separate Claude pass on 2026-10-06 that did not write them (every cited page re-fetched and read for the fact, every answer, wrong answer, explanation and level checked; `checked` keeps who checked it and what was fixed; items that could not be made right, and duplicates of other packs, were deleted). Very easy items are marked difficulty "easy" with "note": "very easy" until the very easy level lands. A person still reviews it by playing. On 2026-10-07 every item whose `source` said "common knowledge" was given a real source instead: a page fetched that day that states the fact, with the supporting phrase quoted in `source.note` (each such item's `checked.fixed` records the change).

review.how: Check every question, answer and explanation. Fix or delete what is wrong, set status to 'reviewed' with your name and the date, then move the file to packs/ and list it in pack_library.js.

items.question: Counting the thumb, how many fingers are on one hand?
items.explain: That makes ten fingers in all on two hands.

source.note: Fetched 2026-10-07; the page says: 'The human hand usually has five digits: four fingers plus one thumb; however, these are often referred to collectively as five fingers, whereby the thumb is included as one of the fingers.'

checked.fixed: source: common knowledge replaced with en.wikipedia.org (2026-10-07)

items.question: Which part of the body do you hear with?
items.explain: Your ears also help you keep your balance.

source.title: Wikipedia: Ear
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'an ear is the organ that enables hearing and (in mammals ) body balance'.

items.question: How many senses are people traditionally said to have?
items.explain: The five are sight, hearing, smell, touch and taste.

source.title: Wikipedia: Sense
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'The five major senses that most higher organisms have are: Sight (vision), Hearing (audition), Smell (Olfaction), Touch (Somatosensation), and Taste (Gustation)'.

items.question: What do people brush twice a day to keep their smile healthy?
items.explain: Most toothpaste contains fluoride, which helps build strong tooth enamel.

source.title: Wikipedia: Toothpaste
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the fact-check pass; the page text contains: 'brushing the teeth' and 'The additional fluoride in toothpaste has beneficial effects on the formation of dental enamel and bones'.

checked.fixed: explain no longer mentions cavities (tooth decay = illness rule); now the fluoride/enamel fact, page-supported

items.question: Which joint bends in the middle of your arm?
items.explain: The elbow sits between the upper arm and the forearm.

source.title: Wikipedia: Elbow
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'The elbow is the region between the upper arm and the forearm'.

items.question: Which joint connects your foot to your leg?
items.explain: The ankle is actually made up of three joints working together.

source.title: Wikipedia: Ankle
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'is the area where the foot and the leg meet' and 'The ankle includes three joints'.

items.question: Which joint connects your hand to your arm?
items.explain: The wrist contains eight small bones called carpals.

source.title: Wikipedia: Wrist
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'Part of the arm between the lower arm and the hand' and 'the carpus or carpal bones, the complex of eight bones'.

checked.fixed: distractor 'The toe' (not a joint) -> 'The shoulder' (same kind)

items.question: Which of these drinks has no calories?
items.explain: Water also helps your body keep a normal temperature.

source.title: CDC: About Water and Healthier Drinks
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the fact-check pass; the page text contains: 'Water has no calories, so replacing sugary drinks with plain water' and 'Water helps your body: Keep a normal temperature'.

checked.fixed: rewritten: 'best for hydration' was not stated by the page and arguable (coffee was a distractor; the page lists plain coffee as a healthier choice); now 'which drink has no calories', which the CDC page states

items.question: A big yawn is often a sign that you are what?
items.explain: Seeing someone else yawn can make you yawn too.

source.title: Wikipedia: Yawn
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'It is commonly associated with tiredness , stress , sleepiness' and 'yawning is often triggered by the perception that others are yawning'.

items.question: What do people wear to block bright sunshine on a summer day?
items.explain: Good sunglasses block the Sun's ultraviolet (UV) rays.

source.title: Wikipedia: Sunglasses
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'wearing sunglasses that block ultraviolet radiation (UV) whenever a person is in the sunlight'.

items.question: What should you wash your hands with to get them clean?
items.explain: Scrub for 20 seconds, about as long as humming "Happy Birthday" twice.

source.title: CDC: About Handwashing
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'Scrub your hands for at least 20 seconds' and 'Hum the “Happy Birthday” song from beginning to end twice'.

items.question: What are the short hairs along the edges of your eyelids called?
items.explain: Eyelashes help keep dust out of your eyes.

source.title: Wikipedia: Eyelash
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'Lines the edges of the eyelids, heightening protection of the eye from dust and debris'.

items.question: What is the rounded back part of your foot called?
items.explain: The heel is shaped by one large bone called the heel bone.

source.title: Wikipedia: Heel
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'Back of the foot' and 'It is based on the projection of one bone, the calcaneus or heel bone'.

items.question: Which curved bones wrap around your chest?
items.explain: Most people have 12 pairs of ribs.

source.title: Wikipedia: Rib cage
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'A typical human thoracic cage consists of 12 pairs of ribs'.

items.question: When you are cold, why does your body shiver?
items.explain: Shivering muscles shake in tiny movements that create warmth.

source.title: Wikipedia: Shivering
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'Skeletal muscles begin to shake in small movements, creating warmth by expending energy'.

items.question: On a hot day, what does your skin make to help you cool off?
items.explain: As sweat dries on your skin, it carries heat away.

source.title: Wikipedia: Perspiration
source.note: Fetched 2026-10-06 by the writing pass; the page text contains: 'Evaporation of sweat from the skin surface has a cooling effect'.

items.question: Which of these is a form of exercise?

source.note: Fetched 2026-10-07; the page says: 'Swimming is a whole body exercise'.
